sections.html:
Haverhill sits on the Merrimack River in Essex County, hard against the New Hampshire line, roughly 35 miles up the road from Boston. The 2020 census counted 67,787 residents, and the 2024 estimate is 68,291. The population grew 11.3 percent between 2010 and 2020, and a growing town tends to keep buyers searching, though no price is promised.

Housing is mostly owner stock mixed with rentals: 26,696 households live in 27,927 housing units, and 4.4 percent of those units were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.8 percent, so hardly any owned homes stood empty.

Buyers sort Haverhill houses by district first, so say which one yours is in. The Merrimack separates the Bradford section from the rest of the city.

  • Downtown: rezoned to encourage artist live-work lofts and educational uses, with a parking garage, boardwalk and boat docks along the river.
  • The Highlands: the district beside downtown, known for Victorian mansions built during the shoe boom.
  • Bradford: across the river, and home to the Bradford MBTA station.
  • Ward Hill and Rocks Village: Rocks Village is a historic district with early architecture, including the 1691 Kimball Tavern.

Winnekenni Park, a conservation area with Winnekenni Castle and Lake Saltonstall, is among the city's best known open spaces. Say so if you live near it.

sections.h2: Older homes and what buyers look at
sections.html:
Haverhill housing runs from colonial-era houses to Victorian mansions and converted mill lofts. Shoe manufacturing built the city, and Bradford joined it on January 1, 1897. Downtown rezoning has turned old factories into loft apartments and condominiums, with about $150 million in public and private investment in the old factory district.

A house that is a few generations old will get a close look at its roof, heating system and basement. Snow loads on roofs, ice dams in gutters and damp basements close to the river are what local inspectors flag most. Keep repair receipts and permit papers handy; they settle questions fast.

Interstate 495 runs through the city with five exits, and Routes 97, 108, 110, 113 and 125 cross it. Routes 108 and 125 end at the New Hampshire line and continue into that state.

  • MBTA Commuter Rail serves the Haverhill and Bradford stations on the Haverhill/Reading Line to North Station.
  • Amtrak also stops at the Haverhill station, with service to Portland, Maine and Boston.
  • MeVa Transit runs local buses in and beyond the city.
  • Logan International Airport in Boston is the nearest international airport.

Commuters ask first about distance to an I-495 exit or a rail station, so have that answer ready.

sections.h2: Tax due dates and late interest
sections.html:
The four yearly installments for real estate and personal property fall on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. Anything unpaid on those dates collects 14 percent interest.

The early bills are estimates built from the previous fiscal year's actual net bill. The city's formula is last year's actual tax times 2.5 percent, added to the actual, then divided by four. Unpaid balances after May 1 can lead to a tax lien, and new liens after November 2024 carry 8 percent interest. Liens are recorded with the Registry of Deeds, which means a buyer's attorney will find it in the title search.

Back taxes are normally paid from your sale proceeds at closing. Get a payoff figure from the collector before you settle on a date.

If a sale happens after the January 1 assessment, the bill remains in the January 1 owner's name. The buyer has to call the Assessors at 978-374-2316 for a duplicate, and your attorney normally divides the year's tax between you in the closing adjustments.

Abatement applications must reach the Assessors on or before February 1. Think your value is too high? Watch that date if you plan to keep the house another year. A quick sale rarely leaves time for an appeal to matter. Current forms and payment options are on the tax payment page.

Before any residential sale closes, the Haverhill Fire Prevention Office checks the smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, under M.G.L. Chapter 148, Section 26F and 26F 1/2. Inspections are done on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and only a limited number can be done each day, so book early.

Units in the buildingInspection fee
One residential unit$50
Two units$100
Three to six units$150
Seven or more units$500

The city will not schedule the inspection until payment is received. You will get an email with the date and a call with the appointment time. Applications and details are on the fire department's page, or call 978-373-8460.

sections.h2: Timing the inspection with your closing
sections.html:
The certificate stays valid for 60 days. Schedule it near enough to closing that it will not expire, yet early enough to swap out a failed alarm. One workable order: sign the contract, request the inspection at once, pay the fee, and file the certificate with your closing papers.

Have the building's age, the unit count and any alarm receipts ready for the visit. If the inspector flags something, fix it and ask about a reinspection.

A thin folder speeds everything up: your latest tax bill, any lien notice, a mortgage payoff statement if you have a loan, and receipts for roof, boiler or electrical work. For an inherited house, add the papers showing who has authority to sign.

Then jot down the street address, the unit count, whether anyone rents a unit, and your target closing date. With those four details a buyer can quote a realistic price and schedule.

Plenty of local sellers hold older houses that need updating, or inherited property they cannot easily manage. Selling as-is for cash suits a house that needs work. It skips the lender appraisal, financing contingencies and most showings, and closing can follow your calendar.

A house in good shape may net more on the open market. Compare what each route leaves you after repairs, carrying costs and waiting time, and have an attorney read any contract first.

faqs.a: Yes. Haverhill is the largest city or town in Essex County, located on the Merrimack River at the New Hampshire border.

faqs.q: When are Haverhill property tax payments due?
faqs.a: Installments fall on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, and late ones accrue 14 percent interest.

faqs.q: How long is a Haverhill smoke detector certificate valid?
faqs.a: Sixty days. Haverhill inspects on Tuesdays and Thursdays and does not schedule until payment is received.

faqs.q: What does a Haverhill smoke and CO inspection cost for one home?
faqs.a: The fee for one residential unit is $50. Two units cost $100, and larger buildings cost more.

faqs.q: Who gets the tax bill after I sell my Haverhill house?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner's name stays on the bill. The buyer asks the Assessors for a duplicate, and closing adjustments split the cost.
